content:
Apple has confirmed it will hold a special product launch event titled "Welcome home" next Tuesday (October 13), but has not yet revealed whether there will be a keynote video. Here's what we know so far.

Apple has not yet confirmed arrangements for the "Welcome home" keynote, but Mark Gurman says there will be an "online video announcement"

Apple has changed its product launch approach this year. The March unveiling of the MacBook Neo was the first example — instead of a traditional launch event, it held an in-person media "experience event" after rolling out other products via press releases over several days.

Now Apple's "Welcome home" event (October 13) appears set to break new ground in the same way.

Unlike traditional events, Apple has yet to add the "Welcome home" event to its Apple Events page, and there are no signs of any livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app.

Things could still change in the days leading up to the event, but current signs point to no keynote video on October 13.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says a video announcement is coming. In a separate article about Apple hosting an event on October 27, Gurman wrote:

According to Gurman — who previously accurately revealed the October 13 date and the event's focus on home products — Apple will roll out an "online video announcement" next week.

The media have been invited to an "Apple Experience" event in New York City, starting at 9am Eastern Time. So if there is an announcement video, it's expected to go live at that time — much earlier than the typical keynote slot.

We expect at least three new products to debut on Tuesday — check out this article for the full rundown.

What do you think — will Apple release a keynote video for the "Welcome home" event? Let us know in the comments.
